mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring threshold conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.0% for three consecutive months, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0% for 3 months, or Rank IC remains negative over 2-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates broad-based weakening in consumer demand, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or interaction Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: During expansionary phases defined by sustained GDP growth (GDPC1 annualized growth > 2.0%), strong demand conditions support corporate earnings and lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 annualized growth > 2.0%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates robust manufacturing activity and corporate capacity utilization, supporting earnings growth and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO rises, or Rank IC remains negative over 2-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: When annualized CPI inflation exceeds 2.5%, it signals persistent inflation that may trigger monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL annualized inflation > 2.5%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a weakening labor market that reduces consumer confidence and spending, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises, or interaction Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles defined by FEDFUNDS rising > 0.5% in 3 months, increased cost of capital reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5% in 3 months, or Rank IC remains negative over 3-year rolling windows.
